summary: Sends script strings over an RS-232 serial connection when input channels meet transition conditions, and exposes simple numeric ASCII input on a return channel.
key_concepts: Serial CHOP communicates through an external serial port using RS-232 style serial settings.
The operator monitors input-channel transitions and sends the corresponding script string through the serial connection.
Any received ASCII numeric digits are reflected on an output channel named return.
Use Serial DAT instead when received data is more complex than simple ASCII numeric values.
Port, baud rate, data bits, parity, and stop bits must match the external serial device.
The Scripts page maps Script sequence entries to input channels and converts supported escape sequences such as carriage return and line feed.

key_params.name: state
key_params.note: Input transition to monitor: off-to-on, while on, on-to-off, while off, or value change

key_params.name: offtoon
key_params.note: Send when the input transitions off to on

key_params.name: on
key_params.note: Send while the input is on

key_params.name: ontooff
key_params.note: Send when the input transitions on to off

key_params.name: off
key_params.note: Send while the input is off

key_params.name: valuechange
key_params.note: Send when the input value changes

key_params.name: script
key_params.note: Script sequence mapped to input channels

key_params.name: script0callback
key_params.note: Script sent for input channel/script index 0

common_gotchas: This CHOP is for RS-232 style serial control through COM ports; USB serial adapters need drivers.
It only reflects received ASCII digits on the output channel named return.
Use Serial DAT for complex received data or arbitrary serial parsing.
Script strings are sent when corresponding input-channel transitions match the State parameter.
Escape sequences such as carriage return and line feed are converted in outgoing scripts.
Match baud rate, data bits, parity, and stop bits to the external device before enabling Active.
Device availability and COM naming are platform/driver dependent, especially for USB-to-serial adapters.
